subject: chinchilla
title: Grab a Chinchilla and You End Up Holding Only Fur

scenes.text: Predators bite down on a chinchilla and end up with a mouthful of nothing.
Chinchillas live high in the Andes, up to five thousand metres, among foxes and birds of prey.
Their fur is absurdly dense, with fifty to seventy-five hairs growing from a single follicle. You have two or three.
When something grabs it, the chinchilla releases a whole patch of that fur on purpose.
Vets call it fur slip. The attacker keeps the fluff, the chinchilla keeps running.
The bald patch can take months to grow back, often in a different shade.

description:
Chinchillas can release a large clump of fur when grabbed or bitten, a defence called fur slip that lets them escape predators.
Their fur is extremely dense, with 50 to 75 hairs per follicle, and the lost patch can take months to regrow.
Which escape artist should we cover next?
first_comment: Chinchillas clean that fur by rolling in dust, not water. Which escape trick is the best in the animal world?
